source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Remove all DIMMs from the system.
2. Power on SUT after BMC is ready.
3. Check SEL occurs POST event: 0xE310 & No DIMM is populated.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. The POST code should match the event.

deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the PostLog entries JSON with the per-entry POST code + description fields so user matches each POST code to its event. No RISK (read-only).

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES covers only a guessed read-only PostLog URI. It does not remove DIMMs, authorize/power the negative boot, establish DIMM/slot identity, prove event 0xE310 belongs to that attempt, decode the vendor code or restore the platform. Its `No RISK` statement ignores physical ESD, service interruption and an intentionally unbootable configuration.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly restores the no-DIMM stimulus, ESD/maintenance gates, bounded boot, full event correlation and DIMM reinstall. This review further requires module-to-slot serialization, power-removal/discharge verification, prohibition on mixed-up channel population, explicit no-memory stop-state/timeout and post-restore inventory/training checks rather than boot-only recovery.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 867/2291 accepts the read-only API command and does not analyze that the actual test requires removing every DIMM, powering an invalid configuration, collecting serial/OOB evidence and safely rebuilding the original memory topology.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1030 draft exists in the invalidated 1,000-record run.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the exact physical stimulus and code; ED-34 treats platform/code/slot data as readiness; ED-35 forbids replacing removal/boot coverage with a log read; ED-38 requires explicit power/hardware approval, recovery, no automatic retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Prove that a deliberate all-DIMM-absent boot attempt produces the platform-defined POST/SEL event `0xE310` whose description identifies that no DIMM is populated, and then restore the exact original memory topology and normal system operation.
original_method: With the SUT fully powered down and BMC available, a qualified operator inventories and removes every DIMM, verifies the empty state, performs one approved power-on attempt, captures the complete POST/SEL interval and then powers down, reinstalls every serialized module in its original slot and verifies memory training, inventory and normal boot. Existing logs are retained rather than cleared.
manual_activity: A qualified ESD-trained operator must remove chassis power as specified, label and remove all DIMMs, verify the empty sockets, authorize/perform the single negative boot and reinstall each exact module in its recorded slot. Automation can capture power/BMC/POST/SEL and post-restore inventory evidence but cannot substitute an API read for the physical stimulus.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/chassis/board/BMC/BIOS identities and vendor confirmation that a no-memory power-on is an approved diagnostic test
Complete DIMM inventory with serial/part/capacity/rank/speed and motherboard socket/channel map plus original photos
Service manual for shutdown, AC/DC isolation, discharge/wait time, ESD, access, latch/removal/insertion order and any torque/air-baffle requirements
Approved maintenance window, no-active-workload/users, stable power, BMC/SOL/serial access, maximum no-POST wait and emergency power-off/recovery owner
Authoritative meaning/encoding/source for 0xE310 and exact expected message, severity, sensor/generator, event direction, boot-attempt/time correlation and acceptable additional events
Post-restore memory training duration, inventory/slot/size/channel checks, POST/SEL health, OS boot and diagnostic acceptance
safety_requirements: Never remove or insert a DIMM while host power is present or before the vendor discharge interval. Confirm AC/DC state independently and follow ESD/chassis service controls.

Do not guess sockets or allow modules to be mixed. Record serial-to-slot placement and physical orientation before removal; stop on unlabeled modules, damaged latches/connectors or an uncertain population rule.

Do not clear SEL, POST or system logs. Snapshot stable record IDs/sequences/timestamps before the one boot attempt so event 0xE310 can be causally correlated without destroying earlier memory-fault evidence.
Do not infer code semantics from the numeric value or a generic `PostCode` field. Use the exact platform/BIOS event specification and preserve raw event data plus decoder version.
Power on only once after explicit approval and BMC readiness; enforce the approved no-memory timeout and never retry automatically if code/message is absent or the platform behaves unexpectedly.

After capture, use the approved power-off path, reinstall every DIMM in its original slot, verify latches/topology and allow bounded memory training. Stop/escalate on missing capacity, new ECC/training errors, boot loop or persistent hardware fault.
agent_execution_scope: Perform read-only identity, power, workload, memory inventory and BMC/POST/SEL baseline checks; present the exact module/slot map and one-boot recovery plan before approval.

After the operator verifies all DIMMs removed, observe BMC readiness and the single approved power-on via OOB/serial, mark the attempt boundary and capture complete new POST/SEL/raw records and power/boot state.
Correlate 0xE310 and its vendor-approved no-DIMM description to this exact attempt, record any extra/unexpected events and enforce timeout without retry.
After operator reinstall, verify hardware inventory, slot/channel/capacity, memory training, POST/SEL cleanliness, BMC and OS health; preserve evidence and never issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the negative boot for this platform, exact code/message semantics, module/slot map, power/ESD procedure, timeout and abort/recovery limits.
Supervise the physical empty/reinstall state and authorize the one power-on plus subsequent safe power-off.
Review causal event evidence and full topology/training/boot recovery, then issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Only a possible post-stimulus evidence query after resource discovery and security correction. It cannot create the required condition, may omit pagination/collection metadata, assumes fields/resource IDs, weakens TLS and exposes credentials; therefore it is not a complete or safe test command.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Execute the vendor-approved physical all-DIMM removal and one bounded boot under operator control, while automation records a stable pre-attempt boundary and retrieves all new POST/SEL raw and decoded events through protected supported interfaces; then restore the serialized slot map and verify complete platform recovery.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All-DIMM removal, BMC-ready power-on, event `0xE310`, `No DIMM is populated`, POST-code/event match Criteria, generic pre-clear, absent Script and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved; no read-only substitution or repeated boot is accepted.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat the case as a single reversible hardware fault-injection transaction: immutable module/slot inventory, safe full removal, one bounded no-memory boot with canonical event capture, controlled power-off, exact reinstall and topology/training/boot recovery verification.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the exact server/board/BIOS/BMC/memory configuration whose service guide and 0xE310 definition approve this stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/BMC/POST decoder, board/memory population specification, service procedure and management client versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform service manual, memory population rules, BIOS/BMC POST/SEL code specification and Project maintenance/recovery plan.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Preserves the physical negative test while adding immutable topology, safe power/ESD controls, causal record boundaries, bounded no-POST behavior and proof of exact hardware restoration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A historical 0xE310 entry or read-only PostLog query is partial evidence only; it does not prove the current all-DIMM stimulus, exact description, power behavior or successful restoration.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Platform authorization, code semantics, DIMM map, power/ESD procedure, maintenance/OOB/timeout and recovery criteria.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Physical handling can damage modules/sockets, mix topology or cause prolonged training/boot failure; a stale event can be misattributed; repeated failed boots may alter diagnostics.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use another approved management interface to retrieve POST/SEL evidence, but must record the preserved Redfish proposal, actual tool/version, reason, engineer approval, equivalent raw/code/description evidence and unverified interface coverage. It may not replace the physical all-DIMM removal and approved boot with historical/read-only evidence and claim full coverage.
expected_evidence: SUT/board/BIOS/BMC identity, maintenance approval, prior power/workload state and complete DIMM serial/part/capacity/channel/socket map with controlled photos
AC/DC isolation/discharge/ESD checklist, qualified operator record and verified all-sockets-empty state before the single power-on
BMC-ready timestamp, explicit boot authorization, power/serial/SOL timeline and bounded no-memory stop-state/timeout
Complete pre/post boundary POST/SEL metadata and raw records showing platform-decoded 0xE310, exact no-DIMM meaning, generator/severity/time and causal attempt correlation
Approved power-off plus serialized DIMM reinstall/latch/slot verification and any chassis components restored
Post-restore memory inventory/channel/capacity, training duration, normal POST/boot/BMC/OS health, new fault-log review, no-retry proof and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target a no-DIMM boot and 0xE310 event/description match. The unsafe blanket pre-clear is a method defect, while platform code semantics and hardware procedures are Project readiness inputs rather than contradictory purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The physical stimulus, expected code and comparison purpose are explicit. Platform approval, DIMM map, code definition, timeout and recovery are supplyable execution inputs, so this is PACKAGE rather than permanent BLOCKED; execution remains forbidden until all are approved.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its critical hybrid classification while strengthening serialized topology restoration, discharge/ESD proof, single-attempt timeout and memory-training/inventory recovery.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-exists reasoning with a qualified-operator fault-injection and full recovery boundary.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents a stale or generically decoded POST entry from passing the case, prevents unsafe live memory handling or module-slot mix-up and requires proof that the platform returns to its exact original memory configuration.
independent_technical_reasoning: The required causal chain is physical absence of all memory, one known boot attempt and one platform-defined 0xE310 record—not simply the existence of that code in a log. Memory service is high-risk because identity and channel placement matter during recovery. Stable log boundaries avoid destructive clearing, while serial-to-slot inventory and post-training checks prove the reversible stimulus did not leave a latent topology or hardware fault.
